title: Device shadow updates with EF Core concurrency tokens
name: Device shadow updater

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code handles concurrent updates to the same device shadow? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
What does the [Timestamp] / IsRowVersion column do in the SQL that EF Core generates when saving a DeviceShadow?
choices: It adds a lock hint so other writers block until SaveChanges completes
It adds the original RowVersion to the WHERE clause of the UPDATE, and the update affecting zero rows is raised as DbUpdateConcurrencyException
It makes EF Core wrap the update in a serializable transaction
It makes the database reject any update that does not change RowVersion explicitly

questions.prompt: TrySetDesiredConfigAsync loads the shadow and then assigns OriginalValue on the RowVersion property from expectedVersion. What does this achieve?
choices: It forces the update to succeed whatever the current database value is
It only affects the in-memory entity and is ignored when generating SQL
It makes the UPDATE fail if the row has changed since the caller read the version it passes in, even though this method loaded the row only just now
It makes the call a pessimistic lock on the row until the caller commits

questions.prompt: Under heavy report traffic from the same device, which statement about ApplyReportAsync is correct?
choices: It can throw DbUpdateConcurrencyException to the caller after the fourth failed attempt
It never throws, because the loop retries until the save succeeds
It holds a row lock for the whole loop, so concurrent callers queue up
It throws InvalidOperationException on the first conflict
